title: Coframe Raises $25M to Personalize Websites with AI
text:

 EN Business & Startups · Tom Levy · November 9, 2026 Coframe Raises $25M to Personalize Websites with AI
 Key Takeaways 1 Coframe raises $25M in Series A, co-led by Khosla Ventures and Hanabi Capital 2 The startup claims over $300M in additional revenue and increased conversion rates for its clients 3 Vinod Khosla criticizes the shopping experience on Amazon and bets on extreme personalization through AI 4 The martech market remains dominated by giants like Adobe and Salesforce Why it matters : Coframe aims to transform web navigation by offering pages tailored to each visitor using AI, in a market where innovation is hindered by established players. Coframe promises pages tailored to each visitor and claims to have generated over $300 million in additional revenue for its clients. The startup, backed by Vinod Khosla, has raised $25 million in Series A funding for its "living internet," in a martech market that its founder believes is dominated by giants.
 Claimed Performance and a Locked Market
 Coframe states that it has enabled its clients to achieve over $300 million in additional revenue, citing conversion rate increases of 158% at Dropbox, 410% at Replit , and 60% at Cash App. According to Josh Payne, the marketing technology sector is largely occupied by companies such as Adobe and Salesforce, as well as numerous providers of testing, targeting, and measurement tools with limited added value. In this context, Optimizely was acquired in 2021 for an undisclosed amount. Payne bets that AI can reinvigorate this category and asserts that "the internet will have its own sense of life," with technology quickly catching up to enable this.
 What Coframe Promises to Do on a Page
 Josh Payne describes current websites as static, designed once and costly to evolve. He clarifies that Coframe's goal is not just to create a more attractive homepage, but to learn what drives a particular customer to click and purchase, in order to provide a more relevant experience that better represents the company and its offerings. Coframe aims to display a page specifically tailored for each visitor and refers to a "living internet." Vinod Khosla emphasizes the extreme personalization made possible by AI and believes that manually coding unique pages would be too slow and expensive.

 Vinod Khosla's Diagnosis of the Current Experience
 Vinod Khosla considers that shopping on Amazon has become cumbersome and claims that the experience has deteriorated over the past 15 years. He argues that the platform promotes what it wants to sell rather than what is most relevant for each user. He believes that standardized websites are reaching the end of their lifecycle.
 $25 Million Raise, Investors, and Project Origin
 Coframe has completed a $25 million Series A funding round, co-led by Khosla Ventures and Hanabi Capital, bringing its total funding to $35 million. The valuation amount has not been disclosed, and Khosla Ventures had previously invested in the company during its pre-seed round. Founded in 2023 by Josh Payne, who studied mathematics and computer science at Stanford and is a co-founder of Autograph, the startup emerged, according to him, from the manual and labor-intensive work observed in consumer activities. With the rise of ChatGPT , Payne saw generative AI as a possible path for the large-scale personalization that Coframe aims to provide.
